summary.text: A 10-year-old Chinese Han boy, the first child of unrelated healthy parents born at full term, had delays in language and personal/social development since infancy, was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder at 5 years old and had three bouts of febrile convulsions at 8 years with no abnormal EEGs. At 5 years, bilateral strabismus with right eyelid ptosis led to a consultation at which myopia, astigmatism and hearing impairment were found, but his mother refused further hospitalization and examination.

During hospitalization at age 10 he had coarse facial features, bilateral strabismus with right eyelid ptosis, facial hirsutism, shin hypertrichosis, fifth-finger distal phalanx hypoplasia, mild clinodactyly, microcephaly and growth retardation. Outside reports gave BCVA 0.3 OD and 0.2 OS, normal IOP and macular OCT, axial length 28.97 mm OD and 30.00 mm OS and ERG dystrophy of cone and rod cells; fundus images showed tessellation changes and auditory brainstem response showed bilateral cochlear damage.

G-band karyotype, chromosomal microarray and fragile X analysis were negative. Trio whole-exome sequencing found a heterozygous missense SOX11 variant, c.1013C>T, p.S338l, that neither parent carried; it was scored likely pathogenic and a genetic diagnosis of Coffin-Siris syndrome 9 was made, alongside a diagnosis of early-onset high myopia.

The guardians declined repetition of the outside ophthalmic investigations because of financial constraints and limited cooperation, so those results rest on outside reports. The authors state that long-term follow-up is still required, noting that a single macular OCT at age 10 does not guarantee lifelong absence of macular pathology.
